record.context_brief: curves meeting a cubic surface at one point
record.original_question: Let S_3 ⊂ P^3 be a cubic surface, let C_d be the family of degree-d curves in P^3, and let D_{S_3,d} = {C in C_d : the support of C ∩ S_3 consists of a single point}, equivalently curves meeting S_3 in one point with multiplicity 3d. Study the geometry of D_{S_3,d}, for example whether it is smooth, irreducible, and of the expected dimension.

evidence.quote: Problem 8 (Ciro Ciliberto) Let S3 ⊂ P3 be a cubic surface. Let Cd be the family of curves of degree d in P3. Study the subfamily DS3,d = {C ∈ Cd : Card(supp(C ∩ S3)) = 1} (in other words, DS3,d is the family of curves intersecting S in one point only, with multiplicity 3d); for instance, it is smooth? irreducible? of the expected dimension? etc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^3$. Let $S_3 \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be a smooth cubic surface, and for each integer $d \geq 1$ let $\mathcal{C}_d$ denote the Hilbert scheme (family) of curves of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^3$. Consider the locus
$$ \mathcal{D}_{S_3,d} \;=\; \{\, C \in \mathcal{C}_d \;:\; \operatorname{supp}(C \cap S_3) \text{ consists of a single point}\,\}, $$
that is, the curves $C$ of degree $d$ that meet $S_3$ in exactly one point, necessarily with intersection multiplicity $3d$ at that point. Investigate the geometry of $\mathcal{D}_{S_3,d}$: in particular, determine whether $\mathcal{D}_{S_3,d}$ is smooth, whether it is irreducible, and whether it has the expected dimension; more generally describe its components, their dimensions and singularities as $d$ varies.
artifact.category_tag: Algebraic geometry of curves on surfaces

It appears as an open problem posed by Ciliberto and no subsequent work specifically addressing the geometry of the locus of degree-$d$ curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ meeting a cubic surface in a single point with multiplicity $3d$ was found.
